t: 2032 — First long-duration swarm coordination testbed runs a sealed swa
title: 2032 — First long-duration swarm coordination testbed runs a sealed swa
definition: 2032 milestone on the Self-Replicating Survey Swarms roadmap.
description:
First long-duration swarm coordination testbed runs a sealed swarm hulls habitat for 1,000 days on Earth, proving the printer bays recycling math.

What must be true first: the printer bays results have to replicate outside the lab, swarm propulsion manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and asteroid mining operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed printer bays demonstrations, swarm propulsion cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting asteroid mining uptime. When all three flash green, 2032 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (6 years from the 2026 baseline.)

definition: Estimates Self-Replicating Survey Swarms readiness from component maturity.

title: Self-Replicating Survey Swarms Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Self-Replicating Survey Swarms operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Self-Replicating Survey Swarms installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 84647 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where printer bays monitoring, swarm propulsion redundancy, or asteroid mining maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Self-Replicating Survey Swarms Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Self-Replicating Survey Swarms: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Self-Replicating Survey Swarms — swarms that build copies of themselves at each star.

Phase 1 — Prove (printer bays): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (swarm propulsion): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (asteroid mining): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (swarm coordination): swarm hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and star systems-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
